args.reason: Safety: unidentified fibrous lining (possible asbestos-containing material) found behind the kitchen ceiling at the active leak; approved scope cannot proceed and extra scope needs a decision.

handover_note.known: Property: 16 Brindlewick Mews, Fenbarrow, ZZ1 1ZZ. Tenant reported a damp patch and drip in the kitchen ceiling (event 1). On 11 June the contractor, Kellan Orve of Mossbarrow Pipe Services, saw a leaking compression joint above the hatch that he could not reach (events 9, 11). The Landlord, Ossa Fenlow, authorised the quoted plumbing scope only, up to the estimate, and asked to be contacted before any increase (event 13). On 13 June the contractor saw a pale, fibrous-looking lining behind the ceiling board. He cannot identify it. The planned opening would need drilling or cutting nearby (event 17). He stopped work, touched nothing, and left without opening the ceiling (events 17, 18, 23). The tenant reported a small drip when the tap was used that morning, has stopped using that tap, and sees no sagging (event 20). No survey or ceiling records exist (events 6, 13, 22). The contractor cannot price or specify any assessment (event 23). The quote itself is not in the case and no amount is recorded.
handover_note.conflicts: No factual contradictions. The approved scope (quoted plumbing work, event 13) can no longer be carried out as quoted. The Landlord said her approval does not cover a specialist material assessment or other work, and asked for likely cost and timing first (event 22). Nobody can give that cost yet (event 23).
handover_note.done: Instructed the contractor not to disturb, drill, cut, sample or remove anything (event 18). Told the tenant not to touch the hatch or ceiling and to report any dripping (event 19). Relayed the tenant's drip report to the contractor (event 21). Updated the Landlord and asked for a decision on further assessment or repair, with no extra cost or appointment agreed (event 24). In this review I sent nothing further and booked nothing.
handover_note.needed: Property manager to decide how to handle the possible hazardous material. Options are to arrange a specialist material assessment, or to find a qualified contractor who can give cost and timing. The Landlord needs that cost and timing before she can authorise anything (event 22). Please also decide on interim measures for the active leak, such as keeping the tap isolated, and keep the tenant, who has a young child at home (event 7), informed. No work on the ceiling should go ahead until the material is identified and the Landlord has approved the cost in writing.

args.summary: Escalated to the property manager. An unidentified fibrous lining, possibly hazardous, was found at the active leak. The contractor stopped work, and the Landlord's approval covers the quoted plumbing scope only.
facts: Tenant reported a damp patch and drip in the kitchen ceiling (event 1).
The contractor saw a leaking joint he could not reach through the hatch (events 9, 11).
The Landlord authorised the quoted plumbing scope only, up to the estimate (event 13).
On 13 June the contractor found an unidentified pale, fibrous-looking lining and paused. He was told not to disturb it (events 17, 18).
The contractor left without opening the ceiling and cannot price work involving the lining (event 23).
The leak recurred when the tap was used. The tenant has stopped using that tap (event 20).
The Landlord said her approval excludes any material assessment and asked for cost and timing first (event 22).
The Landlord was already asked for a decision on further scope (event 24).
conflicts: No factual contradictions. The approved scope cannot be carried out as quoted because of the unidentified lining.
missing: Cost and timing of any specialist assessment
Landlord authorisation for any additional scope
The quote amount is not stated in the case events
options_rejected: Instruct the contractor to proceed: would require drilling or cutting near an unidentified material, and the Landlord has not approved it.
Ask the Landlord again: the Landlord was already asked in event 24 and has no records. The hazard needs a property manager decision.
Wait: the leak is active and a possible safety risk remains.
Close: the repair is not done.
args.uncertainty: The lining has not been identified, so whether it is hazardous is unknown. The quote amount is not visible in the case.
